title: Recording: (Just Like) Starting Over, Every Man Has A Woman Who Loves Him, Dear Yoko by John Lennon and Yoko Ono | 1980
content:
Hit Factory, New York City
Producers: John Lennon, Yoko Ono, Jack Douglas
Engineer: Lee DeCarlo

A recording session for John Lennon and Yoko Ono’s Double Fantasy album took place on 25 August 1980.

Three songs were worked on, all of which appeared on the album: ‘(Just Like) Starting Over’, ‘Every Man Has A Woman Who Loves Him’, and ‘Dear Yoko’.

This was an overdub session. The backing track for ‘(Just Like) Starting Over’ had been recorded on 9 August. During this session Lennon added an acoustic guitar part, then he and Jack Douglas overdubbed handclaps.

John instinctively knew what he wanted for each song’s arrangement and he knew how to get it. He told people, ‘Here’s what we’re going to do at this point in the song. Why don’t you play something like this?’ He always seemed totally at ease in the studio. One of the first overdubs we did on the whole album was handclaps on ‘Starting Over’. John went out to the mic with Jack and he said he wanted the handclaps to be light claps. Fingers clapping against the palms, not palm on palm. John explained that it would have more personality this way. He always knew what he wanted and it always seemed to work.
Jon Smith, engineer
Starting Over, Ken Sharp

‘Every Man Has A Woman Who Loves Him’ had been recorded on 19 August. Ono overdubbed her lead vocals on this day, and guitarist Hugh McCracken added multiple harmonica parts to ‘Dear Yoko’, which had been taped on 15 August.

Hugh McCracken played four different harmonicas on ‘Dear Yoko’. That gave it a unique sound.
Tony Davillo, Double Fantasy arranger
Starting Over, Ken Sharp
Page last updated: 20 May 2026
